clue.text: Girl goes to town, that's the truth

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: A young woman heads for the bright lights, and that is the honest story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to' simply joins the girl's name to the town, which follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Veracity is truthfulness, the quality of being accurate and honest.

clue.text: Food and foreign wine, entertaining a CID man?

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the wine holds the a inside it

parts.note: vin is French for wine
a DS is a detective sergeant, a rank in Britain's Criminal Investigation Department

explanation.surface: A detective is treated to dinner and French wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' puts A inside VIN. The CID is the British police detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Viands is an old word for provisions or dishes of food.

clue.text: Former African island, island with a short name

parts.note: Rhodes is a Greek island
Rhodes is a Greek island
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A one-time African state was an island; another island has an abbreviated name.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhodesia was the former name of Zimbabwe (and Zambia, as Northern Rhodesia).
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Rhodesia, the state now called Zimbabwe, belonged to a nation that no longer exists.

clue.text: Over the limit in prison house

indicators.note: in says the excessive part is placed inside the prison

parts.note: a cage is a prison
OTT is over the top, beyond the acceptable limit

explanation.surface: A drunk driver locked up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over the limit' suggests drink-driving; here it is OTT (over the top).
explanation.definitionFit: A small country dwelling is a type of home.

clue.text: Sweetheart gives short whistle

explanation.surface: A lover signals with a quick blast.
explanation.definitionFit: Toots is a slangy endearment for a darling; toots also means sounds a horn or whistle briefly.

clue.text: Calliope, perhaps, seen by a daughter, was entertaining

indicators.note: the muse is seen flanked by the other two pieces, one on each side, so they sit around it

parts.note: Calliope is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, the muse of epic poetry

explanation.surface: A Greek muse, glimpsed with a girl, was having a fine time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen by' puts MUSE between A and D. The definition reads as 'was entertained': being amused is being entertained.
explanation.definitionFit: To be amused is to be diverted and kept happily occupied.

clue.text: Exotic raiment seen in turret

indicators.note: exotic means strange and foreign-looking, so the clothing's letters take on an unfamiliar arrangement

explanation.surface: Colourful foreign robes on view in a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exotic' rearranges RAIMENT; 'seen in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque, a kind of turret.

clue.text: Bird circling one rustic youth

indicators.note: circling says the bird goes all the way round the numeral

parts.note: a swan is a bird
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bird circles above a country lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' puts I inside SWAN.
explanation.definitionFit: In pastoral poetry a swain is a country lad or young shepherd.

clue.text: Find record has finished

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
over means finished, ended

explanation.surface: Someone notices that the music has stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover is to come upon or locate something.

clue.text: Weariest — whacked, so to speak

indicators.note: whacked means beaten up, so the letters of weariest are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Exhausted: the most tired, completely shattered, you might say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whacked' is British slang for exhausted, which fits 'Weariest', but here it rearranges the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a hedge meaning in a manner of speaking, figuratively.

clue.text: May possibly old fellow stick with ice-creams, say, for a long time?

parts.note: May is one example of a month of the year

indicators.note: say tells us the word for these ice-creams is to be heard rather than spelt as written

parts.note: sundaes are ice-cream desserts with toppings

explanation.surface: Perhaps a man in May has been sticking with ice-cream treats for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns SUNDAES into the identical-sounding SUNDAYS. 'stick with' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means an extremely long period, as in 'not in a month of Sundays'.

clue.text: Radio presenters in loud tuxedos

indicators.note: loud asks for the abbreviation for tuxedos to be spoken out, letter by letter

parts.note: in Britain a tuxedo is a DJ, short for dinner jacket

explanation.surface: Broadcasters turn up wearing garish evening suits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loud' looks like a comment on garish clothes; it asks for DJs (dinner jackets) to be spelt as pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: Disc jockeys host music shows on radio stations.

clue.text: Moving from Troon to city

indicators.note: moving says the letters of the two following words are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone relocates from a Scottish seaside town to a big city.
explanation.walkthrough: Troon is a Scottish golfing town. 'Moving' rearranges TROON into TORON, and TO is added as written; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is the largest city in Canada, capital of Ontario.

clue.text: Know-all leads crew astray round one stretch of water

indicators.note: round says the scrambled crew goes around the other pieces, holding them inside
astray says the letters of the crew are led off course into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a sea is a large stretch of water

explanation.surface: A smart alec takes charge and steers his crew off course over the open sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' rearranges the crew's letters and 'round' wraps them around the other two pieces. 'leads' just links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is a person who pretends to great wisdom, a smart alec.

clue.text: Fellow embraced by animated fiancée — it's very stimulating

indicators.note: embraced by says the fellow is held inside the jumbled fiance
animated means lively and moving, so the letters of the betrothed woman are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A man is hugged by an excited bridegroom-to-be, and it gives him a buzz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animated' rearranges FIANCEE (the accented fiancée lost its last letter in the scan); 'embraced by' puts F inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Found in coffee and tea, it is a stimulant drug that wakes the nervous system.

clue.text: Set of figures put forward for discussion

explanation.surface: A batch of statistics is offered up for debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A table is a grid of numbers; in British usage to table a motion is to propose it for debate.

clue.text: Lose one's nerve, with vessel no longer lit

parts.note: a bottle is a vessel for liquid
a fire or light that is out is no longer lit

explanation.surface: Someone loses courage when the lamp in a jar goes dark.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'bottle' means courage; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The British phrasal verb means to back down from fear at the last moment.

clue.text: Monkey's limb, swathed by doctor, restored to normal alignment

definitions.note: the 's is short for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: swathed by means bandaged by, so the doctor wraps round the limb

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
an arm is a limb
a broken bone that is set has been put back into place

explanation.surface: A monkey's broken arm is bandaged by a doctor and the bone put right.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Monkey's' as 'Monkey is'. 'swathed by' pictures the doctor bandaging the limb, so the limb goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A small South American primate with a long tail is a kind of monkey.

clue.text: Make invalid take answer out of a book

indicators.note: out of, after take, says one letter is removed from the book's word

parts.note: an annual is a book published once a year

explanation.surface: Instructions for cancelling something by removing a solution from a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an annual is a yearly gift book for children. 'take ... out of' removes one A from ANNUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to declare void, cancelling a marriage or contract.

clue.text: He used to swim a lot, and look around

definitions.text: He used to swim a lot

indicators.note: around says the look goes around the word and, holding it

parts.note: to leer is to look slyly or lecherously

explanation.surface: A former swimmer takes in the view as he goes along.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont every night to visit Hero, until he drowned.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary lover crossed a strait nightly, a famous swimmer of Greek myth.

clue.text: Trifling inconvenience making you run about a little

indicators.note: about says the word for run goes around the phrase for a little

parts.note: to flee is to run away
a bit means a little, a small amount

explanation.surface: A minor irritation that has you scuttling around for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A BIT inside FLEE. The surface suggests a bite that makes you itch and fidget.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny itchy bite from an insect is the proverbial minor nuisance, hardly worth complaint.

clue.text: Sprout, from Brussels originally, accompanying egg

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter, the one at the origin of Brussels

parts.note: to egg someone is to urge them on

explanation.surface: A Brussels sprout served alongside an egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' and 'accompanying' link the pieces. 'Sprout' is a verb, not the Brussels vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: To burgeon is to put out new shoots, to begin growing rapidly.

clue.text: Tin over there in a valley

parts.note: a can is a tin
yon is an old word for over there, yonder

explanation.surface: A tin can lying out yonder in a gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep gorge with steep sides cut by a river is a type of valley.

clue.text: Parent's prudent manipulation

parts.note: ma is mother, a parent, and the possessive adds the S
sage means wise and prudent

explanation.surface: Mum's sensible way of handling things.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubdown of the muscles is manipulation of the body by hand.

clue.text: Porthos was heroic, to some extent — inclined to swagger?

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: One of the Three Musketeers was something of a hero, given to strutting.
explanation.walkthrough: Porthos is one of Dumas's Three Musketeers, so swashbuckling fits the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To swash is to bluster or strut, as in the word swashbuckler.

clue.text: Enclosed envelope with follow-up proposal, dropping a line

indicators.note: dropping says the line's letters are let fall from the end of the proposal's word

parts.note: a corollary is a proposition following on from one already proved
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A sealed envelope with a further suggestion inside, minus one line of text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping a line' removes RY (railway) from COROLLARY. The envelope is botanical, not postal.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany this ring of petals is the inner floral envelope surrounding the stamens and pistil.

clue.text: Where to find caught fish? That's about right

definitions.text: Where to find caught fish? That's about right

indicators.note: about says the caught fish surrounds the letter for right

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: An angler asks where the catch goes, and is told the answer is roughly correct.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a fishing basket is where caught fish go.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler's wicker basket holds the day's catch.

clue.text: Before wedding, perhaps, two men act with excessive formality

indicators.note: Before says the two men come ahead of the wedding in the answer

parts.note: Stan is a man's name
Don is another man's name
a wedding is one example of a ceremony

explanation.surface: Before the wedding, perhaps, the best man and usher behave very stiffly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to insist on strict etiquette and fussy formality.

clue.text: Races around gathering endless clothing

indicators.note: around says the races go round the shortened gathering word

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: endless says the gathering word loses its last letter

parts.note: to shirr is to gather fabric in parallel rows, so shirring is gathering
the final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Competitors circle a crowd gathering, all wearing casual tops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the gathering word's last letter; 'around' puts the races round what is left. 'gathering' is a sewing term, not a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-sleeved casual top is a garment, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Timber not seen around — it's floating in the sea

parts.note: a plank is a length of timber

indicators.note: around says the word not is turned round and read backwards

explanation.surface: A piece of wood goes missing, and something drifts in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the word round; 'seen' is a link. The definition paints the drifting organisms as a single floating thing.
explanation.definitionFit: These tiny organisms drift in ocean currents, unable to swim against them.
